products.name: VS Code
products.description: A code editor brings a desktop runtime, a terminal and fast file search into one place to work.
products.contribution: VS Code connects editing, debugging, extensions and terminal sessions into a single developer workbench.
products.scope: Desktop VS Code. Browser and remote editions have different runtime boundaries.
products.unresolved: Exact versions in an installed release depend on its build. Source evidence here is pinned to the inspected repository revision.

products.name: Supabase
products.tagline: A database, with a platform around it.
products.description: Postgres at the center, with APIs and functions that turn a database into an application backend.
products.contribution: Supabase integrates database access, authentication, APIs, a dashboard and managed operations into a backend platform.
products.scope: Hosted platform architecture and documented Edge Functions runtime. Self-hosted deployments may differ.
products.unresolved: Hosted infrastructure and rollout versions are not exposed by these sources. The diagram does not claim a complete deployment inventory.

products.name: OBS Studio
products.description: A production desk that composes scenes, encodes media and brings web overlays into a live broadcast.
products.contribution: OBS adds scene composition, source controls, an audio mixer and the recording and streaming workflow.
products.scope: Desktop OBS Studio with the named plugins enabled. Platform packages and custom builds vary.
products.unresolved: Browser-source and encoder availability depend on the installed build. A foundation shown here need not be used in every recording.

products.name: Firefox
products.description: A browser joins page rendering, JavaScript execution and secure networking into one browsing experience.
products.contribution: Firefox adds tabs, navigation, privacy controls, profiles, extensions and a maintained browser experience.
products.scope: Desktop Firefox. Gecko is an umbrella engine; the selected components describe distinct capabilities, not isolated packages.
products.unresolved: This is a source-level explanation. An installed release, operating system and hardware configuration must be checked separately.

products.name: Blender
products.tagline: From a scene to a finished frame.
products.description: A creation suite connects rendering, color management and movie processing to an artist’s scene.
products.contribution: Blender adds modelling, animation, scene editing and production workflows around rendering and media components. Cycles is developed by the Blender project itself.
products.scope: Desktop Blender with Cycles and FFmpeg enabled. Other renderers and custom builds differ.
products.unresolved: A source build option establishes an available integration, not every shipped binary or selected render device.

products.name: Godot
products.tagline: The tools behind a playable world.
products.description: A game engine connects physics, font rasterization and text shaping to scenes and interactive worlds.
products.contribution: Godot adds the editor, scene system, scripting, resource pipeline and export workflow that turn libraries into a game-making environment.
products.scope: Godot 4.x with Jolt selected for 3D physics and the advanced text server. Jolt entered core in 4.4; defaults vary by release.
products.unresolved: Physics backends and text-server build options vary. This trail does not identify the hardware running a particular game.

foundations.name: Electron
foundations.description: A toolkit for building desktop applications with web technologies. It combines Chromium and Node.js with desktop APIs.
foundations.responsibilities: You supply the interface and application logic, secure the browser-to-system boundary, and maintain packaging and updates.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: xterm.js
foundations.description: A browser-based terminal component. It displays terminal output and accepts input; the shell runs elsewhere.
foundations.responsibilities: Connect it to a shell through a pseudo-terminal or a remote service. Handle process lifetimes, transport, access control and terminal sizing.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: ripgrep
foundations.description: A command-line search tool that searches file contents using regular expressions and respects ignore rules by default.
foundations.responsibilities: Choose search roots and flags, invoke the executable, and present its results. An editor integration also needs cancellation and navigation.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: PostgreSQL
foundations.description: A relational database that stores structured data and runs SQL queries, with transactions and an extensible type system.
foundations.responsibilities: Design your schema and access policies, arrange hosting and backups, and manage upgrades, monitoring and recovery.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: PostgREST
foundations.description: A standalone server that exposes a PostgreSQL database through an HTTP API, using the database schema and permissions.
foundations.responsibilities: Run PostgREST alongside Postgres. Configure database roles, authentication, network access and schema changes.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Deno
foundations.description: A runtime for executing JavaScript and TypeScript outside the browser. Supabase uses a Deno-based runtime for Edge Functions.
foundations.responsibilities: Write and deploy your service, set permissions, manage secrets securely, and arrange routing, monitoring and scaling.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: FFmpeg
foundations.description: Libraries and command-line tools for processing audio and video, including decoding, encoding and container handling.
foundations.responsibilities: Build a media pipeline around the formats you need. Handle timestamps, buffering, errors and the capabilities of your chosen build.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Qt
foundations.description: A cross-platform application framework. Its Widgets module provides desktop controls, layouts and windows.
foundations.responsibilities: Build the application behavior, layouts and accessibility; integrate platform services and package your app. Review the license for your distribution.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Chromium Embedded Framework
foundations.description: Usually called CEF: a framework for embedding Chromium-based browsers inside other applications.
foundations.responsibilities: Integrate rendering, input and browser lifetimes into your application. Maintain the embedded runtime and define its security boundaries.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Chromium
foundations.description: The open-source browser project behind the browser technology embedded by both Electron and CEF.
foundations.responsibilities: Choose an embedding layer such as Electron or CEF, or work with Chromium source directly. Plan for security updates, builds and application integration.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Node.js
foundations.description: A JavaScript runtime with APIs for work outside the browser, including files, processes and networking.
foundations.responsibilities: Supply the application and manage dependencies, permissions, errors and deployment. A desktop interface requires an additional layer.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Gecko
foundations.description: Mozilla’s engine for rendering web content and supporting browser services. Firefox also uses it to render its own interface.
foundations.responsibilities: Building from Gecko means taking on browser integration, release engineering and security maintenance. It is not a drop-in replacement for the complete Firefox application.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: SpiderMonkey
foundations.description: Mozilla’s JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, used by Firefox. Its standalone shell offers access outside the full browser.
foundations.responsibilities: You provide the embedding application, host APIs, lifecycle and security boundaries. The standalone shell does not supply a browser interface.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: NSS
foundations.description: Network Security Services is a collection of libraries for security-enabled applications, including cryptographic and TLS functionality.
foundations.responsibilities: Integrate the library with your networking stack and maintain certificate policy, error handling and updates. A crypto library alone does not secure an application.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Cycles
foundations.description: A physically based renderer developed by the Blender project. It can also be integrated into other software.
foundations.responsibilities: Using the renderer independently means supplying scenes, materials, asset handling and an interface or batch pipeline. Render capacity still needs hardware.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: OpenColorIO
foundations.description: A color-management library for applying configured transformations between image color spaces and display views.
foundations.responsibilities: Supply a suitable color configuration and integrate transforms into your image pipeline. Monitor calibration and consistent asset interpretation remain your responsibility.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Jolt Physics
foundations.description: A C++ library for rigid-body simulation and collision detection, designed to work across multiple cores.
foundations.responsibilities: You integrate object lifecycles, collision shapes, simulation timing and game logic. Godot’s scene nodes and editor workflow do not come with the standalone library.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: FreeType
foundations.description: A library for loading font formats and rendering glyphs. It supplies a building block for readable text.
foundations.responsibilities: Choose and license your fonts, manage glyph caches and integrate drawing. Text shaping and a complete UI layout engine are separate responsibilities.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: HarfBuzz
foundations.description: A shaping engine that turns Unicode text and a font into positioned glyphs, including complex script behavior.
foundations.responsibilities: Provide fonts, segment the text appropriately and draw the shaped glyphs. Shaping does not provide a complete widget toolkit or font rasterizer.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: V8
foundations.description: An embeddable JavaScript and WebAssembly engine. Node.js uses it to execute JavaScript outside a browser.
foundations.responsibilities: Embedding V8 gives you an engine; you supply host APIs, I/O integration, lifecycle management and isolation. Browser APIs are not supplied by V8 alone.
foundations.boundary: No deeper connection has been reviewed for this component yet.

foundations.name: Linux
foundations.description: The kernel manages processes, memory and access to devices. Here, Linux is an explicitly selected execution example, not a claim about every product installation.
foundations.responsibilities: A usable system also needs user-space software, drivers and administration. Running it yourself means managing updates, access, storage and recovery.
foundations.boundary: This trail selects a Linux system on an x86 processor. Other operating systems and CPU architectures are possible; no particular host is identified.

foundations.name: Processor
foundations.description: A processor fetches, decodes and executes machine instructions. This trail uses contemporary silicon processors as its hardware example.
foundations.responsibilities: You can use a local computer or rent compute, but memory, storage, cooling and power still matter. A processor alone is not a usable application platform.
foundations.boundary: The processor vendor, model, fabrication plant and machine behind any visitor or managed service are not identified here.

foundations.name: Transistors
foundations.description: Tiny electronic switches are arranged into circuits that implement processor logic and storage. This trail concerns silicon-based computer chips.
foundations.responsibilities: At this level you are designing circuits, not installing a software dependency. Chip design also requires interconnects, fabrication, packaging and verification.
foundations.boundary: The illustration is conceptual. We do not identify a process node, foundry or transistor design for an actual product deployment.

foundations.name: Silicon
foundations.description: A semiconductor material used as the foundation for the silicon-based transistors in this trail. Manufacturing creates patterned devices on wafers.
foundations.responsibilities: Raw material does not replace a processor. Purification, wafer production, fabrication, packaging and testing require specialized industrial capabilities.
foundations.boundary: The evidence stops at the material. No mine, wafer supplier or fabrication site has been established for these software products.

foundations.name: Electricity
foundations.description: Computing hardware needs electrical energy to operate. Delivering a computing service also involves power conversion, cooling and other supporting equipment.
foundations.responsibilities: Self-hosting changes who manages the machine; it does not remove its energy needs. Consumption depends on the equipment, workload and operating conditions.
foundations.boundary: No utility, generator, energy mix, per-request consumption or electricity price is known for these product examples. Those require deployment-specific evidence.

relationships.provides: Electron gives desktop VS Code a web rendering environment and access to desktop application APIs.
relationships.adds: The editor workbench, extension integration, debugging interface and workspace experience are VS Code’s work.
relationships.scope: Desktop VS Code; not vscode.dev.

relationships.provides: xterm.js provides the terminal display and input surface inside VS Code.
relationships.adds: VS Code connects terminal sessions to the workspace and adds terminal management and shell integration.
relationships.scope: Desktop terminal UI; source revision 2886f6d.
relationships.note: A terminal component is not itself a shell.

relationships.provides: VS Code consumes a packaged ripgrep binary for its file-search implementation.
relationships.adds: VS Code turns matches into a navigable search view, with editor locations, include/exclude controls and cancellation.
relationships.scope: Source revision 2886f6d; package @vscode/ripgrep-universal.
relationships.note: The packaged binary and the upstream ripgrep project are distinct distribution layers.

relationships.provides: Postgres is the database at the center of a Supabase project. You can connect to the database directly.
relationships.adds: Supabase adds a management interface, service integrations and, on the hosted platform, managed database operations.
relationships.scope: Hosted Supabase database; documentation verified 2026-09-14.

relationships.provides: PostgREST exposes database tables and functions through Supabase’s REST API.
relationships.adds: Supabase integrates API access with project configuration, authentication and database policies.
relationships.scope: Supabase REST data API; other API surfaces use different components.

relationships.provides: Supabase Edge Functions execute on a Deno-based runtime.
relationships.adds: Supabase supplies the function deployment workflow and platform integration around that runtime.
relationships.scope: Edge Functions execution only; not the whole Supabase backend.
relationships.note: The managed Edge Runtime is Deno-based; this is not a claim that every Deno API is supported.

relationships.provides: OBS’s FFmpeg plugin links media libraries for codec and container work.
relationships.adds: OBS routes sources through its scene and output pipeline, with recording settings and live production controls.
relationships.scope: obs-ffmpeg enabled; source revision caaa022.
relationships.note: Available codecs depend on the FFmpeg build and OBS configuration.

relationships.provides: Qt Widgets supplies desktop interface primitives used by OBS’s frontend.
relationships.adds: OBS builds its scene list, settings, docks and production controls around its own media engine.
relationships.scope: Qt 6 frontend; source revision caaa022.
relationships.note: Qt provides interface tools, not OBS’s audio/video composition engine.

relationships.provides: The obs-browser plugin uses CEF to render web-based sources and overlays.
relationships.adds: OBS places those browser sources inside scenes and connects their visibility and activity to the production workflow.
relationships.scope: obs-browser plugin enabled; source revision f555da0.
relationships.note: This relationship applies to browser sources and browser docks, not all of OBS.

relationships.provides: Electron embeds Chromium to render application interfaces built with web technologies.
relationships.adds: Electron adds desktop application APIs and integrates the renderer with its application process model.
relationships.scope: Electron architecture; bundled Chromium version varies by Electron release.

relationships.provides: Electron incorporates Node.js for JavaScript work outside the browser renderer.
relationships.adds: Electron coordinates application windows and processes, including the boundaries between renderer and system access.
relationships.scope: Electron main process and permitted contexts; renderer access depends on security settings.

relationships.provides: CEF embeds Chromium-based browser capabilities inside a host application.
relationships.adds: CEF supplies embedding APIs and integration hooks that a host such as OBS can use.
relationships.scope: CEF architecture; browser capabilities and versions follow the chosen CEF build.

relationships.provides: Gecko renders web pages and Firefox’s browser interface.
relationships.adds: Firefox supplies the browsing workflow, tabs and user controls.
relationships.scope: Desktop Firefox; Gecko includes more than the rendering subsystem.

relationships.provides: SpiderMonkey executes JavaScript and WebAssembly for Firefox.
relationships.adds: Firefox supplies browser APIs, navigation and the surrounding application.
relationships.scope: Firefox’s engine, not an external hosted JavaScript service.

relationships.provides: Gecko’s networking uses NSS for cryptography, including TLS.
relationships.adds: Firefox integrates network security with browser identity, permissions and user-facing controls.
relationships.scope: NSS appears within Firefox’s Gecko networking stack.

relationships.provides: Cycles renders scenes when chosen as Blender’s render engine.
relationships.adds: Blender adds scene authoring, animation and the renderer’s artist-facing integration. Cycles is also Blender-developed.
relationships.scope: Inspected source revision with WITH_CYCLES enabled; not the Eevee renderer.

relationships.provides: OpenColorIO supplies color processing within Blender’s color-management system.
relationships.adds: Blender integrates configured views and transforms into its editing and output workflows.
relationships.scope: Inspected source snapshot; color configuration is separate from the library.

relationships.provides: Blender’s movie module links FFmpeg when codec support is enabled.
relationships.adds: Blender connects media processing with its scenes, timeline and output controls.
relationships.scope: WITH_CODEC_FFMPEG build option; codec availability depends on the build.

relationships.provides: Jolt supplies collision detection and rigid-body simulation when selected as the 3D physics backend.
relationships.adds: Godot adds scene nodes, editor controls and integration with game logic.
relationships.scope: Built-in option since Godot 4.4. Applies to Jolt-backed 3D physics, not 2D physics or every project.

relationships.provides: FreeType contributes font rasterization and hinting to Godot’s dynamic-font system.
relationships.adds: Godot supplies font resources, themes and UI controls.
relationships.scope: Godot dynamic-font path; bitmap fonts have different processing.

relationships.provides: Godot’s advanced text server uses HarfBuzz for shaping text.
relationships.adds: Godot combines shaping with font resources, layout and interactive controls.
relationships.scope: Advanced text server; custom builds may use a different text server.

relationships.provides: V8 executes JavaScript within Node.js.
relationships.adds: Node adds I/O, modules and host APIs around the language engine.
relationships.scope: Node.js runtime; V8 alone does not include Node’s standard library.
